source.title: Slaying the Hydra: Interaction-Aware Circuit Discovery in Language Models
source.authors: Sankaran Vaidyanathan; R. Urbaniak; Emily Bunnapradist; Michelangelo Naim; Daniel Waxman

record.tranche_reason: The study uses different, interaction-aware circuit-discovery and evaluation methods to measure IOI component effects and how circuit evaluations depend on metrics. It does not reproduce the original 26-head circuit analysis.
record.gate_note: The study's IOI results include comparisons of primary and backup name-mover scores, a removal evaluation of its estimated 10-head IOI circuit, and comparisons of circuit-ranking overlap and evaluation metrics. Statements about earlier backup-head ablations attributed to Wang et al. are cited prior work, not new results here.
record.test_reason: The study is mainly a circuit-discovery methods paper, but Figure 2 gives its own result on V2 for GPT-2 small IOI. Name-mover heads score 0.14 under plain NIE and 1.16 once downstream witnesses are pinned. That shows downstream heads compensate when the primaries are patched. Figure 7 compares head rankings from different methods on GPT-2 IOI (V4), and Figure 1 shows metric-dependent faithfulness verdicts on GPT-2 IOI (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add that the authors find JuntaLearner beats attribution baselines (EAP, EAP-IG, MAttr) on mean CRS for kill and net, and matches exact per-head NIE. They also find witness pinning helps mainly on Qwen3, not on GPT-2.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces witness-integrated set effects and a gradient-based learner over sets of attention heads; evaluates discovered rankings with faithfulness, kill, net, and CRS rather than reproducing the original 26-head analysis.
record.method_sensitivity: Evaluation summary changes rankings: on Qwen3 SVA, CPR and 1 − CMD favor the late overshooting curve while CRS favors early recovery. Witness pinning also changes primary-versus-backup name-mover scores in GPT-2 IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: On Qwen3-1.7B SVA, CPR and 1−CMD prefer a late, overshooting faithfulness curve (1.01/0.95 vs 0.94/0.94), while CRS prefers the early one (0.59 vs 0.76).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Circuit-quality verdicts reverse depending on the faithfulness-curve summary (CPR, CMD, CRS), across tasks beyond IOI.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing the study's own estimated 10-head GPT-2 IOI circuit kills IOI but also damages other tasks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Discovered IOI circuits are not task-specific; removing them causes collateral damage on other tasks.

record.problems: The study does not directly test backup takeover after ablating primary name movers or validate the original 26-head circuit. Several IOI comparison values are only plotted, and the MIB comparison uses one training seed per cell.

untested.parts: The original 26 heads, their 7 classes and roles, and the faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria are not tested.
No direct ablation of the primary name movers with measured backup activation or IOI recovery. Witnesses are generic downstream heads, not the named backups.
There are IOI runs on Qwen3 and Llama, but no check that the same head classes or roles recur. Reuse of IOI components across tasks is not tested.
There is no comparison of any method's circuit with the original 26-head circuit, and no comparison of ablation types.
The original circuit itself is not re-evaluated across ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
Name orders, templates and prompts with more names are not tested.

missing.what: The 'Alone' bars for the name-mover and backup groups (e.g. 0.41, 0.08), and the per-head values in Figure 2, are not recorded.
Patching the first-layer MLP alone on GPT-2 IOI removes every task and saturates the kill and net curves, so MLPs were excluded from those metrics.
Pinning all eligible witnesses lowers kill, faithfulness and net on GPT-2 (GP z-scores), and especially on IOI (Figure 19, e.g. -7.0).

record.verdict_notes: The record labelled V5 as limits_scope; evidence that metric choice changes the verdict actually supports V5. The Qwen SVA rows and the study's own-circuit removal rows are moved to none. The V2 evidence is indirect: witnesses are sampled downstream heads, and the GPT-2 knob analysis shows pinning hurts scores there. The study cites Wang et al.'s backup finding but does not re-ablate.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the original 26 attention heads in 7 classes, their stated roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.

The study compares causal scores for primary and backup name movers, including with witnesses pinned, but does not report a direct measurement of backup activation or IOI performance after ablating the primary heads.
Although the study evaluates IOI on several models, it does not test whether the same IOI head classes and roles recur across them, or whether components are reused across tasks.
The study compares selected rankings and evaluation metrics, but does not establish whether other ablation types recover the original circuit's head classes and roles.
The study compares evaluation metrics and reports collateral damage, but does not systematically test the original circuit across prompt distributions or ablation types.
It does not compare IOI name orders, templates, or prompts with more names.

tranche.reason: Uses witness-integrated causal scoring and a learned set-based discovery method to investigate compensation and circuit recovery.

source_check.notes: V2 evidence concerns downstream compensation, without identifying which heads take over name moving. Figure 7 provides qualitative ordering agreement, not a direct comparison with the original circuit; claims about other studies were outside this check.

statements.problem: The MAttr overshoot finding is correct, but the conditions incorrectly describe this study's MAttr circuits as edge circuits.
